headline: GMO tells customers to disconnect PCs after breach; PHP2Shell CISA deadline is tomorrow; PeopleSoft zero-day was three chained flaws

bullets.text: New: Japan's GMO told customers to shut down and disconnect their PCs from the internet following a data breach and ransomware threat (4 outlets). GMO is also offering a $1 million bounty over its FX trading cloud breach.

China-linked hackers are exploiting PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) to root firewalls. It leads at 8 outlets and CISA's federal due date is tomorrow, 2026-10-29. Fixes are in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35.
New: the Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day exploited by ShinyHunters turns out to be three chained flaws, including CVE-2026-35273 (3 outlets).
CISA warns that hackers are now exploiting the critical Node2Shell flaw. Treat it as active exploitation and follow vendor guidance for fixed releases.

Adobe Commerce PolyShell attacks have breached hundreds of stores as Brotli exploit traffic emerges; CVE-2026-48356 (Magento) and Brotli CVE-2026-111497 are in CISA KEV, due 2026-11-10. Adobe also fixed 8 critical Campaign Classic flaws.

Breaches: Northern Territory Health backtracked on its claim that only five patients were hit by the RDH breach; Bithumb, So-net (2.6M records) and 123 Reg disclosed breaches; ransomware still disrupts UNM Health. The LiteLLM 1.107.0 compromise remains on the board.

actions: Update PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 before CISA's 2026-10-29 deadline, including firewalls and appliances, and check exposed hosts.
If you run Oracle PeopleSoft, follow Oracle's guidance for the chained flaws including CVE-2026-35273 and review access logs for signs of compromise.
Find any Node2Shell-affected systems you run, apply the vendor's fix now and check exposed hosts for compromise.
Patch Adobe Commerce/Magento for CVE-2026-48356 and Brotli CVE-2026-111497; check stores for webshells and unexpected uploads.
Apply Tailscale's SSH fixes on nodes that use Tailscale SSH.
Search lockfiles, images and CI caches for litellm 1.107.0; if it ran, treat the host as compromised and rotate every credential it could read.
